label: copy-phase re-fed token (esp. first copied token z/w/t/digits) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phase), and only on re-fed tokens (in_first=0), almost entirely in long sequences (L=9 holds 81% of mass, L=8 17%, L<=5 none). The main mode, 63% of mass, is the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx=1), where the input is orig(0). Magnitude depends strongly on which token that is: z gives the top activations, followed by digits 2/1/0, w and t; ordinary letters give weak activations. A smaller second mode sits at the last few copy steps of length-9 sequences (recall_idx 6-8), again favouring z/w/t/digit inputs. The best single predicate, recall_idx==1 & L>=8 & input in {z,w,t,0,1,2}, scores dev F1 0.44 (precision 0.64, mass recall 0.48). Broader predicates covering both modes reach about 0.95 mass recall but only about 0.07 precision, so the selectivity within copy steps of long sequences is only partly captured.
